title: Exploratory analysis: distributions, relationships and first hypotheses

videos.script: Fourteen lessons made the data trustworthy. This one starts using it. {{start}} Exploratory analysis is asking the clean data simple questions and looking hard at the answers. What is typical. What is unusual. What moves together. What changes over time. {{questions}} The answers here are real, and some are surprising. Orders come in two waves, one before lunch and one after dinner. {{hours}} December brings a third more household revenue than November, before the clinics and offices are even counted. {{december}} And from July, every bag of sugar sold costs more than ten times what it did in June. {{sugar}} Exploration does not prove any of this. It ends with hypotheses: statements precise enough to be wrong, and a note of what would show that they are. {{hypotheses}} That is the hand-off to the next course. A chart is only as honest as the question behind it. {{end}}
